site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records transcribed from the NCG Guidelines for Gynaecological Cancers (2019) (National Cancer Grid, India), the epithelial ovarian cancer section ('Work Up & Investigations' text and the summary table of imaging and management recommendations: Essential (a), Optimal (b), Optional (c)), each with its verbatim quote under where (the Word file has no page numbers). Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' or 'proposal' (clinical_history, histopathology, gi_endoscopy, mammogram_bilateral) are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). A record NCG gives only under a condition the system never judges (an age, a finding, a plan) is shown with NCG's own tier and the condition, never counted. Epithelial ovarian cancer only: borderline, germ cell and sex cord-stromal ovarian tumours have their own sections of the book and are not covered here. The FIGO stage is the stage as recorded by the clinician, never computed. Nothing here suggests treatment.
settings_note: Setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes stage). The three settings follow the rows of the book's summary table, 'Early Stage I/II', 'Locally advanced Stage III/IV' and 'Recurrent' (the treatment algorithm splits 'Clinical early stage' and 'Clinical advanced stage', and relapsed disease).
